identity.title: DOUBT: Decoupled Object-level Understanding and Bridging via vMF-based Trustworthiness for Hallucination Detection in MLLMs

problem.claim: Detect hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), whose image- or fact-contradicting assertions undermine reliability in high-risk applications.

gap.claim: Joint image-text detection can overestimate trustworthiness and miss hallucinations when weak visual understanding causes repeated but incorrect answers.

contributions.claim: DOUBT, a model-agnostic hallucination-detection method combining decoupled object-level understanding and bridging with vMF-based trustworthiness.
A two-step OUB prompting scheme separates object recognition from relational reasoning, followed by reasoning grounded in identified objects.
A von Mises–Fisher-based trustworthiness metric intended to be more stable than semantic entropy in small-sample settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present DOUBT as a simple, model-agnostic approach that combines OUB with vMF-based trustworthiness for hallucination detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the vMF-based trustworthiness metric is more stable than semantic entropy metrics in small-sample settings.
The authors report that experiments and ablations across multiple benchmarks show DOUBT consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, with reported robustness and generalizability.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLM hallucinations conflict with images or facts and threaten reliability in high-risk uses.
Existing joint image-text consistency approaches may miss hallucinations because repeated incorrect answers inflate trustworthiness estimates.
DOUBT decouples object recognition from relational reasoning through OUB and adds a vMF-based trustworthiness metric.
The authors report consistent gains over state-of-the-art baselines across multiple benchmarks and ablations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates object identification from relational reasoning and pairs that decomposition with a trustworthiness metric designed for small samples.

lessons.interpretation: Decomposing a failure-prone multimodal judgment into intermediate perceptual and reasoning checks can make the source of uncertainty more explicit.
lessons.application: For a multimodal reliability method, define separate object-level and relation-level checks, then report how each contributes to the final confidence estimate.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when the task requires holistic visual interpretation or when intermediate object labels are unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract gives no benchmark names, dataset sizes, numerical gains, or statistical uncertainty for the reported comparisons.
The claimed robustness and generalizability are not further qualified by model families, tasks, or distribution shifts.
